header.title: Particle Burst
header.description: Confetti, spark, or star burst on click. Particles fly from the exact point you pressed, in a decorative layer (`pointer-events: none`) that doesn't block the child. `trigger` picks a single burst per click (`click`) or repeated bursts while pressed (`hold`), and `variant` picks the look (`confetti`, `spark`, `star`). It uses the Particles layer, so it needs `particles.css`.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Combine props, click the button, and see the generated code. `interval` only applies with `trigger="hold"`.
playground.label: Celebrate

base.title: Basic burst
base.description: With the defaults (`variant="confetti"`, `intensity="md"`, `duration={900}`) each click throws `18` paper bits from the point you pressed. If you activate the button with Enter or Space, the burst comes from the center. The root is an `inline-flex` `div` with `overflow: visible`, so particles leave its edges: keep room around it and avoid containers with `overflow: hidden`.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: `confetti` is paper rectangles that spin and drop a little with gravity. `spark` is thin glowing streaks aligned with their flight. `star` is four-point sparkles that pop and fade.

image.title: On an image
image.description: The burst works over any content. The layer has `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events: none`, so it doesn't interfere with alt text or clicks. Click different spots on the image.

hold.title: Press and hold
hold.description: With `trigger="hold"` bursts repeat while you hold and follow the pointer as it moves. `interval` is the time between bursts (minimum `40` ms). The pointer isn't captured, so the button gets its click on release. With `asChild` on the button, holding Enter or Space also repeats bursts from the center until you release the key or focus leaves. The root sets `touch-action: none` and `user-select: none` so touch doesn't scroll or select text.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: `colors` takes a palette and each particle takes the next color, in order. `color` is a single color, used when `colors` is omitted. Without either, each variant uses its default palette. Prefer tokens.

spread.title: Spread
spread.description: `spread` is how far particles travel, in pixels, and wins over `intensity`. Each particle travels between `45%` and `100%` of it; with `confetti`, gravity adds `35%` downward.

count.title: Count
count.description: `count` sets particles per burst (from `1` to `80`) and wins over `intensity`. They spread in a circle with a slightly random angle.

duration.title: Duration and delay
duration.description: `duration` is how long each particle takes, in milliseconds. `delay` postpones the burst; each particle also adds up to `70` ms at random so they don't all leave together.

intensity.title: Intensity
intensity.description: Without `count` or `spread`, `intensity` sets both: `10`, `18`, or `28` particles traveling `56`, `88`, or `128` px for `sm`, `md`, or `lg`. It also takes a number from `0` to `1`.

asChild.title: On a button (asChild)
asChild.description: With `asChild`, the burst goes straight onto the gem-system `Button`, without an extra `div`. The position is measured against the button itself, and Enter or Space on the button throws the burst from its center. With a void element like `` or ``, which can't have children, the effect falls back to the wrapping `div`.

state.title: Paused and disabled
state.description: `isPaused` freezes the particles on screen and blocks new bursts. The timer that removes them pauses too: they stay put until you resume, and `outParticleBurst` waits for them to finish. `isDisabled` skips bursts and keeps the content interactive. Here each particle lasts `2400` ms so you have time to pause it.

callbacks.title: Events
callbacks.description: `onParticleBurst` fires on the first burst (or when a hold starts) and `outParticleBurst` when the last particles finish, with the reason in `event.reason`. Each burst counts as active for `delay + duration`: while that lasts or particles remain, repeated clicks don't fire `onParticleBurst` again. With reduced motion no particles are drawn, but the events still fire. The inner button still gets its click: `pointerdown` bubbles up to the root. If you activate it with Enter or Space, the burst comes from the center and the events fire the same way.

texts.body: Click the button (or activate it with the keyboard): it bumps the counter and throws the burst.

header.title: ParticleBurst API
header.description: Reference for props, inheritance, accessibility, CSS classes and variables, and exported types of `ParticleBurst`.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: Playground and examples for each variant, trigger, and option.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from `@gem-org/gemffects/particle-burst` with `particles.css` (the particles) and `particle-burst.css` (the root), or from the package root if you already load `styles.css`.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> (except color) and forwards them to the root div (or the child, with asChild). onPointerDown, onClick, onKeyDown, onKeyUp, and onBlur run before the effect's internal logic. style reaches the root unchanged: the effect writes no variables on it.

items.reducedMotion: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce no particles are created; the child stays the same. onParticleBurst and outParticleBurst still fire: each burst counts as active for delay + duration, even if nothing is drawn.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: ignoreReducedMotion (or the gemfx-ignore-reduced-motion class on an ancestor) keeps the bursts. Use it only when motion is essential.
items.decorative: The layer has aria-hidden and pointer-events: none: it isn't announced and doesn't block clicks. If the burst confirms an action, also say so in text.
items.keyboard: Activating a focusable child (button, link) with Enter or Space throws a burst from the center and fires onParticleBurst. If the root is the focused element (with asChild on a button, or with tabIndex), Enter and Space throw bursts too, and with trigger="hold" holding the key repeats them until you release it or focus leaves.
items.touch: With trigger="hold" the root sets touch-action: none, so touch can't scroll starting from the effect. disabledOnTouch ignores touches and restores touch-action: auto; mouse and pen keep working.

items.variant: Active variant. It has no styles of its own: each particle's class sets the look.
items.hold: Added with `trigger="hold"`. Sets `user-select: none` and `touch-action: none`. The pointer is tracked with listeners on `window`, without capturing it, so children get their `click`.
items.paused: Added with `isPaused`. Pauses particles with `animation-play-state`; the timer that removes them pauses in JS.
items.inactive: Added with `isActive={false}`. Hides the particles on screen.
items.surface: Wraps the child (`z-index: 0`). With `asChild`, the class goes on the child itself.
items.layer: Particles layer (`position: absolute`, `inset: 0`, `z-index: 1`, `aria-hidden`). `--burst` sets the easing and end scale.
items.particle: Each particle. The variant class sets the shape: radius for `confetti`, glow for `spark`, and a four-point `clip-path` for `star`.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: The duration is written inline on the layer and per-particle values go inline on each particle. The motion ones come from the layer class.

items.particleDuration: Duration of each particle. Set by `duration` and inline on the layer; to override it from CSS, declare it on `.gemfx-particle`.
items.motion: Easing (`--gemfx-easing-exit`), initial vertical offset (`-50%`), and end scale (`0.35`). Set by `.gemfx-particle-layer--burst` and overridable with a class.
items.particle: Origin, travel, rotation, size, color, and delay of each particle. Computed in JS on every burst.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Global variables ParticleBurst reads as defaults. Palettes are only used when you pass neither `colors` nor `color`.

content.title: Content
content.description: What the particles burst over and where the effect mounts.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: Duration, delay, and interval, in milliseconds.

state.title: Trigger and state
state.description: When it bursts, how it pauses, and how it turns off.

items.asChild: Applies the effect to the single child, without a wrapping `div`. With void elements like `img` it falls back to the `div`.
items.variant: `confetti` is paper bits, `spark` glowing streaks, and `star` four-point sparkles.
items.colors: Particle palette; each particle takes the next color. Prefer tokens.
items.color: A single color. Used when `colors` is omitted.
items.count: Particles per burst (`1` to `80`). Wins over `intensity`.
items.spread: How far they travel, in pixels. Wins over `intensity`.
items.delay: Delay before the burst. Each particle adds up to `70` ms at random.
items.trigger: `click` throws one burst on `pointerdown` (or Enter or Space); `hold` repeats them while the pointer or key is pressed.
items.isActive: Allows new bursts. When `false`, hides the particles on screen.
items.isPaused: Freezes the particles on screen (and the timer that removes them) and blocks new bursts.
items.isDisabled: Skips bursts; the child stays interactive.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: Throws particles even when the user prefers less motion. Only when essential.
items.disabledOnTouch: Ignores touch pointers; mouse and pen keep working.
items.onParticleBurst: Fires on the first burst or when a hold starts. Also with reduced motion, even if no particles are drawn.
items.outParticleBurst: Fires when the last particles finish and `delay + duration` has passed since the last burst (with `hold`, release waits for them) or on unmount.
items.ref: Ref to the root (the `div`, or the child with `asChild`).
